title: AI That Sees & Hears
hook: Early chatbots only read and wrote text. Today's AI is 'multimodal' — one system can look at a photo, listen to your voice, and reply in words or pictures, the way people switch senses.
key_points: Multimodal AI handles more than text: images, audio, and sometimes video together.
You can show it a photo and ask about it, or talk to it and have it talk back.
It works by translating every input into the same internal 'language' of numbers.
This is why one assistant can describe a picture, then write about it — no separate tools.
content_html: The first chatbots lived in a world of pure text — you typed, they typed back, and that was the whole conversation. A big part of why AI suddenly feels so much more capable is that it broke out of that box. Modern systems are multimodal, meaning a single model can handle more than one kind of information: you can show it a photo and ask "what's wrong with this plant?", point your camera at a math problem, speak to it and hear a spoken reply, or ask it to read a chart and then write a summary. It's a bit like the difference between a pen pal and a friend sitting across the table who can also look at what you're showing them and talk out loud.
extra_html: The trick that makes this possible is elegant. Rather than bolting separate tools together, a multimodal model learns to translate every type of input — words, the pixels of an image, the waveform of a sound — into the same internal "language" of numbers. Once a picture and a sentence live in that shared space, the model can reason across them as fluidly as it once handled text alone. That's why a single assistant can look at your fridge, suggest a recipe, and then write you a shopping list, without you ever switching apps. It's also the foundation under the friendlier, more natural AI experiences arriving now — voice assistants you can actually converse with, tools that understand a screenshot, and glasses or phones that can describe the world in front of you. The same cautions still apply (it can misread an image as confidently as it can misstate a fact), but the leap from "text-only" to "sees and hears" is a big reason AI feels less like a search box and more like an assistant.

related.title: Generative AI
related.hook: The AI behind ChatGPT and image generators doesn't look up answers — it predicts what plausibly comes next, one piece at a time, until it has built a whole response.

related.title: AI Images, Art & Video
related.hook: Type a sentence, get a picture. Image generators learned the link between words and visuals from billions of captioned images — which is also why artists are raising hard questions.

related.title: Voice Assistants
related.hook: Siri and Alexa could set a timer; the new voice AIs can hold a real conversation. Talking is becoming a normal way to use AI — handy, natural, and always a little bit listening.

flashcards.prompt: What does it mean that AI is 'multimodal'?

choices.text: One system can work with several kinds of input — text, images, audio
It can run on multiple phones at once
It only works in multiple languages

flashcards.explanation_html: Multimodal AI isn't limited to text — the same model can take in pictures, sound, and words together, and respond across those forms.

flashcards.prompt: How can one AI handle pictures, sound, and text together?
flashcards.back_html: It converts every kind of input into the same internal numerical representation, so it can mix and reason across them with one model.
